sections.h2: What does the Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court record?
sections.html:
The clerk records and indexes real estate in Forsyth County: deeds, plats, condominium floor plans, UCC filings, General Execution Docket entries, lien filings and military discharges. When you sell a house in Cumming or anywhere else in the county, the deed to your buyer ends up in this office, and so does the cancellation of the security deed once your loan is paid off.

The Real Estate division answers at 770-781-2120 (choose option 6) or at RealEstate@forsythco.com. The clerk's letterhead gives the courthouse address as 101 E. Courthouse Square, Cumming, GA 30040. The clerk's site also offers a property index search, a forms page, a link to the state fraud-alert service for property and mortgage records, and a map viewer for abstractors.

sections.h2: How much does the Forsyth County clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A deed, quit claim deed or similar real estate document costs $25.00 to record, and extra pages are included. Security deed cancellations, releases and assignments are also $25.00 each. The table below repeats the lines most sellers meet at closing, taken from the clerk's posted schedule.

Selected Forsyth County clerk fees (Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court, Court Costs and Recording Fees)
ItemFee
Deed, quit claim, modification, assignment of leases and rents (each)$25.00, added pages included
Security deed cancellation, release or assignment$25.00, added pages included
General Execution Docket or lien filing$25.00
UCC filing$25.00
Certified copy$2.50 first page, $0.50 each added page
Regular copy$0.50 per page
Copy needing staff help$1.00 per page
Copy larger than 8.5 by 14 inches$2.00 per page

Ask the Real Estate division to confirm the total before you mail a check, because the schedule covers the clerk's fee only. Transfer tax and any intangible recording tax are separate charges.

sections.h2: How is Georgia transfer tax handled when a Forsyth County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The tax has to be paid before the clerk will record a deed, and the clerk then attaches a certification that it was paid. The Georgia Department of Revenue sets the rate at $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price and 10 cents for each further $100 or fraction of $100. The statutes are O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10.

By default the seller owes it, though purchase contracts often move it to the buyer, so read your settlement statement to see who paid. The PT-61 declaration is completed online through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, and the clerk's menu links straight to that filing page. For questions about whether a particular transfer is taxable or exempt, the Department of Revenue tells people to call the county clerk.

sections.h2: What is the intangible recording tax on a mortgage?
sections.html:
It is a separate state tax that falls on lenders and borrowers, not on a seller handing over a deed. The Department of Revenue says the holder of a long-term note secured by real estate must record the security instrument in the county where the property sits within 90 days. The rate is $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the note's face amount.

In most Georgia counties the clerk collects it, and in a few the tax commissioner does. Your settlement statement shows whether any of it applies to your closing.

sections.h2: How does e-filing a deed work in Forsyth County?
sections.html:
The clerk's site sends real estate e-filers to efile.gsccca.org. Since January 1, 2025, anyone who files real estate documents electronically there must upload government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport, and have it verified before the filing can go forward. The portal cites O.C.G.A. 44-2-39(b)(1) for that rule.

Closing attorneys and title companies handle this routinely. If you plan to bring a deed yourself, call the Real Estate division and ask which filing methods it accepts for your situation, plus how your payment should be made out. The clerk's FAQ page lists questions about checks, card payments, witnesses and notarizing, so check it before you drive to the courthouse.

sections.h2: How do liens, tax executions and unpaid property tax connect to the clerk?
sections.html:
Unpaid county property tax can turn into a lien called a Fi.Fa., and the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner says these are recorded on the General Execution Docket kept by the clerk. A Fi.Fa. stays in effect for seven years, and paying the taxes plus fees, penalties and interest cancels it. The tax office sends a 30-day notice of intent before it issues one.

  • A lien on the docket is a public record, so expect it to be raised when the buyer's side searches title.
  • The cancellation is itself a filing at the clerk's counter, with the lien fee shown in the table above.
  • Tax sales, when scheduled, are auctions held on the first Tuesday of the month at the courthouse in Cumming.

The tax commissioner's property tax page also asks sellers to email the closing statement to the tax office so the next bill goes to the new owner's name, provided the purchase closed before November 15.

The PT-61 filed with the clerk does a second job for the buyer. When the property was not subdivided, changed or improved and the transfer tax was paid, the tax commissioner says that form can stand in as the new owner's property tax return, and the preceding year's final valuation is treated as the returned value unless a new return is filed with the Board of Assessors.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of a recorded Forsyth County document?
sections.html:
The clerk's Copy Requests page lists three prices tied to O.C.G.A. 15-6-77: standard copies at 50 cents a page, certified copies at $2.50 for the first page and 50 cents for each additional page, and non-standard copies at $1.00 a page. Non-standard means unscanned, odd-sized or atypical records that need hands-on help from staff.

You can also search the property index on the clerk's website to see whether a cancellation of your old security deed was filed. If it is missing, call your loan servicer first and then the Real Estate division.

sections.h2: What should a Forsyth County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts counts 282,805 residents in Forsyth County as of July 2025, up 12.5 percent from the 2020 base, spread over about 224.62 square miles of land. It lists 98,879 housing units, and 84.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $550,400 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and median household income was $143,784.

With values that high, a clean deed and a paid-up tax account matter a great deal to a buyer's lender. Cumming is the county seat and the clerk's office sits in the courthouse there.

  • Median gross rent in the same survey was $2,090.
  • The county issued 1,743 building permits in 2025.
  • About 22.9 percent of residents are foreign-born, and 27.7 percent speak a language other than English at home.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a house in Forsyth County?
faqs.a: The Real Estate division of the Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court in Cumming. Reach it at 770-781-2120 (option 6) or RealEstate@forsythco.com.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Forsyth County?
faqs.a: The clerk's posted fee is $25.00 for a deed, quit claim or similar real estate document, with added pages included. Transfer tax is billed separately under O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and following.

faqs.q: Who owes the Georgia transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under the Department of Revenue's description, although many contracts shift it to the buyer. It must be paid before the clerk records the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need ID to e-file a real estate document in Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Since January 1, 2025, anyone e-filing real estate documents through the Georgia clerks' portal must upload government-issued ID and pass verification first.

faqs.q: Can an unpaid tax bill stop my Forsyth County sale?
faqs.a: It can complicate it. A tax lien recorded on the clerk's General Execution Docket shows up in a title search, and it stays on the docket until the taxes, fees, penalties and interest are paid. Ask the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure before closing.
